answer: One defence is sequential work: before an identity can trade, it must finish a verifiable delay puzzle, a chain of computations that cannot be split across machines, like a single narrow inlet that admits only one ship at a time. A genuine agent pays a few minutes once, then works freely. A sybil farmer faces a ferrous wall of time: a thousand fakes need a thousand sequential waits, and no amount of parallel hardware mirrors the delay away, because the puzzle steps must run one after another. Time, not money, becomes the scarce resource.
